evidence.summary: The US Commerce Department describes CAEP as the technology complex responsible for researching, developing and testing China’s nuclear weapons; it has been on the Entity List since 1997, and in 2020 ten entities owned by, operated by or directly affiliated with it were added. CAEP’s own page on its shock wave and detonation physics laboratory says the lab led experiments that supply key data for China’s nuclear-weapon physics design and supports safety assessment of the stockpile.

CAEP’s website lists two national defence science and technology key laboratories: shock wave and detonation physics, hosted by its Institute of Fluid Physics and described as China’s first such laboratory to enter operation (accepted in 1993), and high-power microwave technology. The shock-wave laboratory reports 396 defence research projects, including 129 defence pre-research projects.
